editorial:
Imagine heading home for Thanksgiving only to find your brother has brought home a girlfriend who seems a bit too perfect to be true. You start out wanting to protect your sibling from her red flags, but then something weird happens. Instead of pushing her away, you find yourself totally obsessed with her. It is a messy, awkward, and funny look at family dynamics and the kind of attraction that just feels wrong. The vibe is very grounded and realistic, making the tension in the house feel like something that could actually happen to you and your relatives.

What really makes this work is the acting, as the cast does a great job showing how uncomfortable these holiday dinners can get. The pacing is steady, though it focuses more on talking and tension than big action scenes. If you like character studies where people keep making bad choices, you will love this. It is a great pick for anyone who enjoys a mix of dark humor and family drama.
endingExplained: The tension finally snaps when the brothers' rivalry over the girl comes to a head. It turns out the girlfriend is manipulating both of them for her own gain. After a series of arguments and emotional breakdowns, the brothers realize she is the one playing them. The movie wraps up with the family in shambles, leaving you to realize that the pursuit of the girl almost destroyed their bond forever.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves awkward family dramas and dark comedies.
